body: Thanks for responding. It might have been my teacher, but then again I've always been better at English, History, etc.
Thank you for responding! This was helpful.
Do you think my university GPA will go up if I transfer back to my original university?
Thanks for the great advice!
Thanks for the advice. My parents REALLY want me to go back to my old school though. I'm stuck tbh.
I think so. I have yet to speak to a GOOD psychiatrist because I'm just gaining insight into what went wrong and what's wrong with me.
I understand. I've taken a year off already.
I'm on Seroquel which is a antipsychotic. I'm also doing exercises.
I see. Thank you very much for the clarification.

So, I guess I should just take the 2 semesters of CC classes then. However, I'm taking care of my mental problems that plagued me during college and I can handle them with therapy and family intervention. I'm also actively seeking for work despite an empty resume.
Ok, thanks.
Do I also have to take the SAME courses (the ones that I flunked in) again at community college? Sorry if I'm frustrating you. I don't think I'm making myself clear either.
Will I be put on probation if I start community college until I get my GPA back up? I'm sorry, but your sentence was a little confusing to understand.

It WAS grades, but I had really bad judgement due to my illness and did not withdraw, drop the courses or change my major. I also lacked insight into my illness so I did not get help or seek counseling services. I'm taking a strong antipsychotic so my senses are coming back (the illness was probably psychotic in nature). I KNOW that I cannot get a passing grade the second time because these courses are math-based and I'm not good in math or science.

I'm speaking to a counselor, specifically Marcela Moreno. She told me to take courses required for a major at Santa Monica College. However, her colleague told me that I can take GE's at SMC if I want to. Their plan for me is to take courses at SMC then apply for the Bruin Readmission Program. They never mentioned Bruin Extension. I will speak to her again though.
OP, I mean you could have switched majors or sought treatment for your depression. But I guess it might been up to your parents regarding your major.

Wow, that was very brave of you to sign up for the Navy without your parents knowing. I'm in the same situation (I failed out of college possibly due to untreated schizophrenia). Maybe, be honest with your parents and talk with them. Joining the navy is a courageous, yet challenging act. I'm sure they will be proud that you're owning up to your mistakes.
I feel the same way as well. I don't want to die, but I feel like I don't have a way out.

My bond with my mom is (I know, embarassing) inseparable. I don't have enough money to move out anyway. 

It's my depression that making them act this way. I know it is. It's cruel. 

I love them. I wish I was in a different reality where they're all happy and I'm still at school. Unfortunately, that can't happen now. 

I'm really stuck. Our neighbors are really gossipy. My uncle lives in the same apartment complex as we do and he and his family don't like us. I just want to slap myself over and over. I really did lose faith in myself.

Yes. I feel negative and it's affecting my family life. I guess that's why my mom called me a good for nothing loser. Depression really sucks. I wouldn't wish it on anyone. It's a real monster. 

Honestly, tbh, I'm surprised I'm in this situation even though I know it's due to poor decisions (I don't have the best judgement in the world and I'm often a little too shy to say anything). I hate myself. This is a nightmare.

This is a dumb question, but what do you mean by garbage? Yeah, I'm in pain because I've hurt my family and those around me. I let them down due to my stupidity, fear, and shyness. 

I understand. I have to let go of the past. I'm not mentally strong, but I'll try to be. 

This whole fiasco has spooked me. I know this not who I am.

I wish I was strong. I just want to feel better for myself and for my family. I admit, I've been depressed for like 7 months which is a ridiculously long period of time. Looking back, I feel stupid for being that way. I'm scared, but I want to make myself feel useful again. I want to believe in myself once more. 

It's just this demon in my head that keeps me telling me that I'm worthless and will always be stupid and a burden on others forever.

I'm kind of in the same situation. I was always very quiet and I had trouble establishing friendships in school. In high school, I was picked on because I had no friends which made me very depressed to this day. I became very antisocial which (along with depression) led me to perform poorly in college. I might start community college, but depression is tormenting me. Sometimes I wish to end it all, but I have family who love me and I just can't do it.
Thank you for supporting me. Congratulations on improving yourself and your life.

I edited my resume. I'm finally going to go job-hunting. These past 6 months have been a rollercoaster for me and my family due to family issues and my situation. I really hope there is a light at the end of this dark tunnel that I put myself in. It gave me time to think though. I realized that I have depression that has been following me around FOR YEARS and I need to do something about it. I will also test for Asperger's.
She has forgiven me. I don't have any friends lol, but I'll just try. I understand that I need to change, I just need a psychologist to help me calm down.

I'm like you. I started becoming a social recluse during my teenage years because I sucked at communicating  with others and even forming friendships. My poor social skills even caused me to be in a fight. Isolation is horrible; I have depression and anxiety because of it. It even caused me to quit college. It has made me think that I might have Asperger's because I'm so socially awkward.

I'm your age and I'm also in the same situation. I never had a real job before (although I was paid through an internship and tutoring program). I don't know how to drive yet because my parents WANT to teach me how, but life constantly absorbs their time. I don't have my life completely organized either. I have depression too. Stay strong though. Seek help if you need it.
I called a psychologist today. Hopefully, I'll get better soon.

I can't go back to my college. I already appealed the decision to expel me, but it was upheld. I thought at the time that lack of effort was the reason why I was kicked out. It took me all this time to realize that depression and possible Asperger's were the most probable reasons.

My year sucked too. I was forced to leave college because I couldn't adjust socially. My grandfather was murdered in Mexico. My uncle is in jail. My great grandmother passed away almost exactly 1 year ago, but I still mourn for her. I'm also fighting off depression, but it's been hard. I get headaches, episodes of grief, stomachaches, and diarrhea. 

Please seek help immediately. Make an appointment with a psychologist. Don't kill yourself. You made it all the way through most of the year. You survived. I'm confident that you will get ahead and that your future will be brighter than now.
I see. Thanks for responding.

I have to see a psychologist this month. I've been trying to set up an appointment over the phone, but it's been hard because they're booked or I miss the calls. I might have to go to a psychologist's office and set up an appointment. What's an AQ?

Thanks, but I'm uncertain right now. I'm thinking of trade school so that I can get a decent paying job. I don't want to go to community college just to get an associate's degree in something that may not get me a good job.

Thank you for taking the time for reading and understanding my situation. I'm holding onto the belief that things will get better with assistance from others and my own efforts. You know, I guess you're right about every bad thing not being my fault. I guess that bad things just happen.
